article.title: Latest OTT releases (July 20-July 26): 19 new movies and TV shows on Netflix, Prime Video, JioHotstar and more - Vogue India
article.summary: Latest OTT releases (July 20-July 26): 19 new movies and TV shows on Netflix, Prime Video, JioHotstar and more Vogue India
article.full_text: It’s time for your weekly update of the latest OTT releases and the next seven days have the perfect blend of movies and TV shows to satiate all your bingeing needs. Kay Kay Menon plays a laid-back headmaster who will stop at nothing to win a government-sponsored Cambridge trip by turning around his city’s most dysfunctional school in Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya; Vikrant Massey, Vedika Pinto and Mahima Makwana star in Musafir Cafe, a romantic drama about three strangers whose unplanned meetings across Bhopal and Mussoorie alter the course of their lives; Kevin Hart crashes a Miami bachelor party he was accidentally added to via group text in the raucous comedy 72 Hours; comic book store owner Stuart Bloom accidentally triggers a multiverse Armageddon after breaking a device built by Sheldon and Leonard in Stuart Fails to Save the Universe, the latest spin-off set in The Big Bang Theory universe. The third season of this backstage WWE documentary series takes viewers inside the writers’ room as the company builds toward WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas. John Cena appears in the final months of his in-ring retirement tour, while AJ Lee makes her long-awaited return. The season also tracks the rise of next-generation superstars Trick Williams, Oba Femi and Bron Breakker alongside established names Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, CM Punk, Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Chelsea Green, Lash Legend, Stephanie Vaquer and Matt Cardona. This feature documentary follows the story of a couple in a well-to-do California suburb who, shortly after getting married, begin receiving threatening emails from a mysterious sender calling themselves ‘LilithIsTruth.’ All signs point to the husband’s ex-girlfriend, who is subsequently arrested, but as the investigation deepens, it becomes increasingly unclear who is the true victim and who is the true villain. From the creators of Ganglands, this eight-episode French thriller follows David (Tomer Sisley), a senior GIGN chief who believed his field days were behind him. When an unknown enemy armed with stolen military-grade explosives launches a series of attacks targeting the unit itself, David is forced back into active command. He must simultaneously protect Max (Tristan Zanchi), his 25-year-old godson and the son of a fallen colleague, who has just joined the unit against David’s wishes. Inspired by the real-life case of Elize Matsunaga, who murdered and dismembered her husband Marcos Matsunaga in their São Paulo apartment in 2012, this Brazilian psychological thriller fictionalises the events leading to the crime. Lorena Comparato plays Elize, a former escort who discovers her wealthy husband’s infidelity and is slowly consumed by betrayal. Henrique Kimura plays Marcos, with Miwa Yanagizawa, Julia Shimura and Denise Weinberg in supporting roles. A Mexican medical drama, My Daughter's Father, follows the desperation of a doctor searching for a kidney donor for her critically ill daughter. What begins as a race against time triggered by a medical emergency soon unravels into something else as he uncovers a secret affair and a DNA test that threatens to shatter two families. The second live-action adaptation of Mattel’s iconic franchise—following the 1987 film starring Dolph Lundgren—follows Prince Adam (Nicholas Galitzine), who crashed on Earth as a child and spent 15 years separated from his Sword of Power, his only link to his home planet of Eternia. When the sword leads him back, he returns to find Eternia under the fiendish rule of Skeletor (Jared Leto). To save his family and his world, Adam joins forces with Teela (Camila Mendes) and Duncan/Man-At-Arms (Idris Elba) and embraces his destiny as He-Man. Alison Brie plays Evil-Lyn, James Purefoy stars as King Randor, Morena Baccarin plays the Sorceress, Charlotte Riley plays Queen Marlena and Kristen Wiig voices Roboto. Bill and Tom Kaulitz, the twin brothers and founding members of Tokio Hotel, return for a third season of their intimate reality series. This season splits its time between Los Angeles, Berlin and the Hanover hometown where they grew up. Both brothers offer rare personal reflections on their childhood, the marks their environment left on them and the new chapters currently unfolding in their personal and professional lives. Tom’s wife, Heidi Klum, features alongside the brothers. Nour Al Ghandour leads this Arabic romantic comedy as Haya, a woman who has kept her best friend Jawad (Ali Kakooli) firmly in the friendzone for years. When Jawad announces his engagement to Zeina (Noha Nabil), an actress and social media personality, Haya realises she may have miscalculated and sets off on a mission to win him back. This Thai action-thriller zeroes in on Num (Nadech Kugimiya), a former underground debt collector released from prison and facing a terminal illness, who attempts to leave that world behind. When he witnesses a brutal debt collection carried out by Po (Daou Pittaya Saechua), the violent son of a notorious loan shark, he is pulled back in and forced to protect the victims of an illegal lending network in what may be his final fight. Chaiwat Thongsang co-stars. Set six months after Season 1, rancher Staten Kirkland (Josh Duhamel) is fighting to reclaim his family’s Double K Ranch after losing the trusteeship, while musician Quinn O’Grady (Minka Kelly) returns from the New York Philharmonic to a hometown she once tried to outrun. A new romantic complication arrives in the form of Oliver (Ben Robson), while land rivalries and family legacies continue to fracture the community around them. Patricia Clarkson joins as Quinn’s mother Claire O’Grady. Lizzy Greene, Garrett Wareing, Marianly Tejada, Jack Schumacher, Casey W. Johnson and Brett Cullen return. Based on Jodi Thomas’s bestselling novel series. Joe (Kevin Hart), a 40-year-old advertising executive whose career is in free fall, is accidentally added to the group text of a bachelor party he has no connection to. Rather than leave the chat, he joins the group for a three-day trip to Miami, hoping the wild weekend will salvage both his confidence and his career. Marcello Hernández, Mason Gooding, Kam Patterson, Ben Marshall, Zach Cherry, Michael Mando, Mike Epps, Andy Garcia and Teyana Taylor round out the cast. Gyaneshwar Tripathi (Kay Kay Menon) is the laid-back headmaster of one of Delhi’s most dysfunctional government schools. When he learns that the headmasters of the city’s ten best-performing schools will be sent on a government-sponsored training programme to Cambridge, he sets out to transform his school against every conceivable obstacle. These include unruly classrooms, scarce resources, indifferent parents and a staff of teachers with their own complications. Archana Puran Singh, Naveen Kasturia, Abhimanyu Singh, Deven Bhojani and Prachee Shah also star. Set across Bhopal and Mussoorie, the eight-episode series follows three strangers whose lives become unexpectedly entwined. Chander Mohan Sharma (Vikrant Massey) is searching for a life that feels genuinely his own. Sudha (Vedika Pinto) is building her future entirely on her own terms. Preeti (Mahima Makwana) provides a quiet, steady presence as the three navigate love, loss and the decisions that alter their paths. Adil Hussain, Rajeev Siddhartha, Anubha Fatehpuria, Loveleen Mishra and Sadia Siddiqui feature in supporting roles. Based on Divya Prakash Dubey’s novel. The fourth television series set in The Big Bang Theory universe and the second direct spin-off of the original sitcom, Stuart Fails to Save the Universe picks up when comic book store owner Stuart Bloom (Kevin Sussman) accidentally breaks a device built by Sheldon and Leonard, triggering a multiverse Armageddon. Now tasked with restoring reality, Stuart is joined by his girlfriend Denise (Lauren Lapkus), geologist friend Bert (Brian Posehn) and quantum physicist Barry Kripke (John Ross Bowie), encountering alternate-universe versions of familiar Big Bang Theory characters along the way. Washed-up former tennis prodigy Dusty Boyd (Jake Johnson) has been reduced to coaching unruly children at his father Chuck’s (Ed Harris) suburban country club. He desperately seeks his father’s approval while supporting Chuck’s vendetta against the growing pickleball craze. When Dusty reaggravates an old injury that takes tennis away from him entirely, he reluctantly takes up pickleball as rehabilitation and, guided by his new partner Candace (Mary Steenburgen), discovers he actually enjoys it. Forced to choose between two worlds, Dusty confronts old ghosts, including childhood nemesis Andy Roddick, who plays himself. Ben Stiller, Patton Oswalt, Chloe Fineman, Chris Parnell, Aaron Chen and John McEnroe round out the ensemble. Ruth (Stéphanie Magnin), estranged from her family for years, returns home after her mother dies under suspicious circumstances. There, she is reunited with her father, Martín (Jose Coronado), who, since retirement, has become aggressive, erratic and consumed by a sinister conspiracy theory. His behaviour is so alarming that Ruth begins to suspect he may have been responsible for her mother’s death. Saravanan (Arjun Das) and Mithra (Anna Ben) appear to be an ordinary middle-class couple running a small hotel in Mulki, Karnataka, caring for their differently-abled son Jeeva. When Jeeva is kidnapped by a government official seeking revenge, the investigation reveals that the couple are, in fact, highly skilled con artists with a carefully buried past, forcing them to pull off one final high-stakes con to get him back. Yogi Babu, Vadivukkarasi, Radha Ravi, Thambi Ramaiah, VTV Ganesh and Aruldoss feature in supporting roles. Set against the politically charged landscape of 1957 Kerala, when the Communist government’s Land Reform Bill triggered fierce tensions between landlords, settlers and the church, the film follows Krishna Pillai (Tovino Thomas), an orphan raised by an adoptive family who arrives in the village of Kaaniyar under an assumed name and is appointed as the church’s protector. As hidden loyalties surface and ideological battles escalate, the man behind the assumed identity is forced into a reckoning that could alter the fate of the entire community. The fourth and final Cour of the acclaimed Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War adaptation brings one of anime’s longest-running franchises to its long-awaited conclusion. Picking up directly from Part 3’s finale at the Soul King Palace, Ichigo Kurosaki and his allies face the ultimate confrontation with Yhwach at full power, a battle that will determine the fate of every realm. Ichigo’s newly awakened Horn of Salvation form, fusing his Hollow and Quincy powers, is the season’s defining visual set-piece. creativeDirection.dramaticPremise: On the eve of an early-morning departure, two flatmates fight over one final show, but the week's 19 new OTT releases turn a simple binge into an impossible choice.

dramaticSpine.characterGoal: Asha wants to watch exactly one short episode before sleeping, while Kabir wants to begin a fresh OTT binge.
dramaticSpine.obstacle: They disagree over whether to finish their current show or gamble on a new release, and the clock is already running late.
dramaticSpine.newsCatalyst: The July 20-July 26 OTT update brings 19 new movies and TV shows across Netflix, Prime Video, JioHotstar and more.
dramaticSpine.reversal: Every title Kabir pitches creates a bigger argument, until Asha realises the choice itself is consuming the only time they have.
dramaticSpine.costOfFailure: Asha loses sleep before her early departure and Kabir loses their planned movie night to indecision.
dramaticSpine.emotionalTurn: Their competitive arguing softens when both admit they want the same thing: one memorable night together, not a perfect catalogue choice.
dramaticSpine.resolution: Asha takes the remote, chooses Musafir Cafe, and Kabir agrees to stop browsing after one episode.

visualBible.setting: A cramped animated Mumbai flat living room at night, with a sagging sofa facing a television, an open suitcase near the door, and rain-glossed apartment windows.
visualBible.colorAndLighting: Warm mustard lamp light against cool blue monsoon light from the windows; the palette shifts from restless orange to calmer lavender by the ending.
recurringProps: black streaming remote with a cracked red button
two mismatched mugs on the floor
visualBible.storyArc: The room begins cluttered and frantic, becomes a comic battlefield around the sofa and remote, then settles into shared quiet as the two friends finally commit to one programme.

cast.role: Flatmate desperate to start something new

cast.visualIdentity: Lanky Indian man in his late twenties, maroon T-shirt, round glasses, striped lounge trousers, oversized popcorn bowl held like a trophy.

beats.dramaticAction: Kabir blocks Asha from switching off the television by planting himself in front of it and waving the remote.
beats.turningPoint: Asha learns the July 20-July 26 OTT update has made their one-show plan suddenly much harder.

visual.caption: Nineteen new OTT releases, one exhausted sofa.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film frame, Kabir theatrically blocking the television while holding a black remote with a cracked red button, Asha reaching around him with one hand and gripping her half-packed yellow suitcase with the other, cramped Mumbai living room, low three-quarter camera, mustard lamp and blue rainy window light, comic urgency, recurring popcorn bowl and mismatched mugs visible, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: Continuous opening shot in the living room as Kabir physically interrupts Asha's bedtime shutdown.
visual.continuityNotes: Establish Asha's green kurta, yellow suitcase, Kabir's maroon shirt, remote and popcorn bowl; no position changes except Kabir stepping into her path.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.text: The July 20-to-26 OTT releases are here—nineteen new movies and shows. You cannot kill the evening now.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.text: I can, Kabir. My suitcase is packed, and sleep is also a very strong series.

beats.dramaticAction: Kabir snatches the popcorn bowl before Asha can carry it away and pitches titles while hopping over the suitcase.
beats.turningPoint: Asha's simple one-episode plan becomes a frantic contest between incompatible choices.

visual.caption: The remote becomes a tiny battlefield.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film frame of Kabir hopping over the open yellow suitcase while rescuing the oversized popcorn bowl, Asha lunging for the remote, sofa cushions skewed, rainy Mumbai flat at night, dynamic side camera, warm lamp streaks and blue window glow, playful desperation, recurring mugs and clothing details, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The argument physically moves around the sofa as Kabir turns the room into a comic obstacle course.
visual.continuityNotes: Continue directly from the previous blocking pose; suitcase remains open by the door, remote stays in Kabir's hand, popcorn bowl now raised above his head.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.text: Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya: Kay Kay Menon's headmaster fights to win a Cambridge trip. Or 72 Hours—Kevin Hart crashes a Miami bachelor party.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.text: You heard ‘one episode’ and invented a film festival.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.text: There is also Musafir Cafe. Three strangers, Bhopal to Mussoorie, romantic complications. That sounds efficient.

beats.dramaticAction: Asha wrestles the remote free, but Kabir catches her wrist before she can press the power button.
beats.turningPoint: The factual size of the slate overwhelms their original plan, and neither can pretend browsing is saving time.

visual.caption: Nineteen choices. Zero progress.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film close two-shot, Asha gripping the cracked-button remote while Kabir gently catches her wrist, both frozen mid-argument beside the sagging sofa, popcorn suspended in the bowl, Mumbai rain beyond the window, low intimate camera, split warm-cool lighting, disbelief and comic tension, recurring suitcase and mugs, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The tug-of-war stops the room completely; the news fact lands as the cause of their paralysis.
visual.continuityNotes: Remote passes from Kabir to Asha; keep Kabir's hand on her wrist and preserve the skewed cushions and open suitcase from the prior shot.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.text: Nineteen. Not three. We have spent twelve minutes choosing a title.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.text: Fine—Stuart Fails to Save the Universe. He breaks Sheldon and Leonard's device and triggers a multiverse Armageddon.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.text: Wonderful. Even Stuart saves reality faster than we choose television.

beats.dramaticAction: Asha drops onto the sofa and sets the remote on the cushion; Kabir reaches for it, then notices her alarm already ringing from the suitcase.
beats.turningPoint: The immediate cost becomes real: continuing the search threatens Asha's sleep, so Kabir must choose between more options and the shared night.

visual.caption: The perfect pick is costing them the night.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film frame, Asha collapsing onto the sagging sofa as a small alarm glow spills from the open yellow suitcase, Kabir frozen with his hand hovering over the remote, popcorn bowl lowered, intimate Mumbai living room, over-the-shoulder camera, lavender-blue rain light mixing with fading mustard lamp, tender comic tension, recurring mugs and wardrobe, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The frantic search turns into a quiet deadline when Asha's early departure intrudes on the argument.
visual.continuityNotes: Remote rests on the sofa between them; Asha is seated, Kabir stands beside her, and the suitcase remains open with the alarm sound implied visually.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.text: My alarm is already judging us.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.text: Then one episode. No trailers, no scrolling, no ‘maybe this one.’

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.text: I am surrendering my right to make it worse.

beats.dramaticAction: Asha presses play on Musafir Cafe, places the remote inside her suitcase, and nudges the popcorn bowl toward Kabir.
beats.turningPoint: They trade endless choice for one shared commitment, ending the argument without pretending the 19-release slate has disappeared.

visual.caption: One choice is enough for tonight.
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film final frame, Asha calmly placing the black cracked-button remote inside her yellow suitcase while Kabir settles beside her and accepts the oversized popcorn bowl, two mismatched mugs near their feet, rain-soft Mumbai window, intimate front camera, gentle lavender and mustard lighting, relieved affectionate mood, clear caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: Final continuous shot: Asha commits to the choice and the two friends settle into the first episode together.
visual.continuityNotes: Continue from the sofa arrangement; alarm glow fades, remote leaves the cushion for the suitcase, and Kabir shifts from standing to sitting beside Asha.

lines.speaker: Asha
lines.text: Musafir Cafe. One episode. If three strangers can survive unplanned meetings, we can survive a choice.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.text: And next week, I am preparing a spreadsheet.

story.exit: Asha zips the suitcase with the remote inside, and Kabir finally stops browsing as the two friends share the popcorn in the glow of one chosen story.
